summary.headline: Vardhman sees industry spinning spreads near $0.90–0.95/kg versus ~$0.60–0.65 four months ago, but Q4 hit by ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market loss.
summary.overview: Management described a sharp turnaround in the Indian textile value chain over the past six months: US tariffs eased, cotton and yarn prices rose, and Chinese yarn demand lifted Indian exports. Q4 gross margin rose about 300 bps QoQ, but EBITDA was held back by an other-expense charge of about INR57–58 crore from mark-to-market on rupee forward cover after the rupee hit INR94.80 on 31 March. Management said fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, so Q4 did not fully reflect the improvement and Q1 FY27 should be better. The call gave no formal numeric guidance; most outlook comments were qualitative and tied to cotton, the dollar-rupee rate and the FTA pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ, as stated by analyst; management did not dispute

financial_highlights.metric: Forex mark-to-market loss charged to other expenses
financial_highlights.change: Q4 one-time hit; rupee at ~INR94.80 on 31 March
Up from ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier; management cited 40–50% improvement

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: 30s combed yarn rose from ~$2.65–2.70/kg in Nov–Dec to ~$3.30–3.35/kg now. Management said yarn prices are set by international cotton and demand is strong, and that spinners are sold about 2–3 months forward in exports.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Management said fabric price hikes are being pushed selectively, with a 2–3 month lag to yarn. The new performance (100% synthetic) fabric plant, commissioned last fiscal year, is expected to reach full use in 6–9 months.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Small existing garment capacity is being expanded to improve viability. Management said there is no decision on a large-scale garment expansion. Average realisation per shirt was stated as $7.5 after an initial misstatement of $5.

guidance_outlook: Management expects most textile companies, including Vardhman, to do far better in Q1 FY27 given the spread improvement, and said Q2 and Q3 should beat last year if current yarn prices, rupee and cotton levels hold.
Remaining ~10% of spinning modernisation to finish in the next 6–8 months; biomass boilers and other green power projects to commission in 1–2 months, with cost benefits from June or July.
Forex mark-to-market will reverse or add depending on where the dollar-rupee closes; no forecast was given.
Cotton: Vardhman normally holds 6–8 months of cotton cover; new Indian crop arrives around October, so stocks must be run down by September.
Management expects FTA-driven demand to build over roughly 12–15 months and is finalising capacity plans over the next 2–3 months.
capex_capacity: Spinning modernisation about 90% complete; remaining work to finish within the current financial year (next 6–8 months).

Performance fabric plant commissioned last fiscal year; 6–9 months needed to build order book. A fourth cotton and normal fabric line was also commissioned in FY26 but could not be fully used because of US tariffs; utilisation is expected in 6–9 months.
Open-end spinning project on hold to restart. New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh is expected by December or January, with plans to be finalised in 2–3 months.

Industry spindles: about 53 million rated; 11–12 million permanently stopped, leaving about 41–42 million working (industry estimate, not government data). Normal additions of 2–2.5 million per year were missed for three years.
Garment capacity expansion approved as a first step to viability; no decision on broader expansion.
demand_pricing: Chinese buying of Indian yarn rose to ~30 million kg per month over the last 4–5 months, against 7–8 million kg earlier. India's monthly yarn exports reached ~120 million kg-plus against a 100 million kg average.

Cotton: New York futures rose from ~$0.62–0.63/lb to ~$0.82–0.83/lb. Indian cotton moved from INR52,000–53,000/candy to INR67,000–68,000/candy; CCI selling price was INR67,000/candy after a ~INR5,000 rise in the last week.
Indian cotton is now priced around New York plus $0.05–0.08, close to the long-run relationship. Management said this removes the earlier disadvantage for spinners.

Pricing: fabric and garment price increases are being pushed across the chain. Brands are granting only small increases so far, with management expecting more clarity in 1–2 months. Yarn cost pass-through was described as comfortable given stronger demand.

Management noted US garment and home textile utilisation has recovered to roughly 90–100% after tariffs eased, from 50–60% earlier. Earlier, US tariffs reached 50%, which had forced discounting and loss-making orders.

qa_highlights.question: How has the cotton price move to parity with US cotton affected yarn demand and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn prices follow international cotton and that higher Indian cotton cost is absorbed by Indian producers. Demand and higher cotton costs have been passed on comfortably so far.

qa_highlights.question: Can the spread gains be quantified and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the spread at ~$0.90–0.95/kg against ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier, about 40–50% higher. Sustainability depends on New York futures and China demand, which management could not predict.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin expansion limited despite gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market charge at INR94.80/USD on export hedges was booked in other expenses. Management said the reversal depends on the year-end rupee rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 fabric lag mean stronger Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, and Q1 should be better, with Q2 and Q3 also better than last year if spreads hold.

qa_highlights.question: How long will spindle capacity take to return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects expansion decisions in 6–9 months if margins hold for 3–6 months. About 1,000 small mills have closed, so consolidation is structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for garments and realisation per shirt?
qa_highlights.answer: Garment capacity expansion is an early viability step with no decision on broader expansion. Realisation was given as $7.5 per shirt.

risks_watch: Forex: Q4 carried a ~INR57–58 crore mark-to-market loss; Q1 reversal depends on where the dollar-rupee closes.
Cotton price durability: a fall in New York futures would compress the current spread. Hedge and speculative flows were cited as a source of volatility.
Policy: the government has not decided on duty-free cotton imports. Ministry support was described as aligned but unconfirmed.
Fabric pass-through lag and brand resistance to price increases.
Geopolitics: the Iran–US conflict has raised crude and logistics costs and affects polyester pricing; China's demand for Indian yarn may not last.
Spread and capacity figures are industry estimates (not government data) and could be revised.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat about the industry cycle, with spreads, capacity exits and FTA demand as the main positives. Cautious and evasive on sustainability: management repeatedly said New York futures, China demand and the war were beyond its control and declined to give forward numbers or a cotton purchase cost.

growth.why: Management gave no numeric guidance, only qualitative comments that Q1 FY27 and Q2/Q3 should beat last year on a sharp rise in yarn spreads (~$0.90-0.95/kg vs ~$0.60-0.65 four months ago), backed by pricing pass-through, Chinese yarn demand and a few already-commissioned lines still ramping, with Q4 EBITDA held back by a ~INR57-58 crore forex mark-to-market charge.
